english.title: Wear uniform signifying association with political organisation in public
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wore a uniform signifying your association with

(A)_[a political organisation,]_(B)_[the promotion of a political object,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ORGANISATION OR OBJECTIVE..),

(C)_[in a public place,]_(D)_[at a public meeting,]_
namely, **(..DESCRIBE PLACE OR MEETING..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and 7(2) of the Public Order Act 1936.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
wore a uniform signifying his / her association with
a political organisation / the promotion of a political object
in a public place / at a public meeting

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: An offence is not committed where the chief officer of police, with the consent of a Secretary of State, by order permits the wearing of such uniform. See subsection 1(1) .

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
